data.name: Atalia
data.gender_notes: Atalia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Atalia means 'God's answer'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'atalet', which means 'answer' or 'response'. In the Bible, Atalia is not mentioned directly, but it may be connected to the name Athalia, which is mentioned in the Old Testament. The name Atalia carries the meaning “God's answer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Atalia usually hope their child will grow to embody god's answer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes hope and faith, representing God's response to our prayers and desires.
data.etymology: Atalia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's answer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atalia total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: עֲטָאֲלִיָּה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עֲטָאֲלִיָּה: הַנְּשִׂיא, שָׂרָא, אֹתִי, אֵין פְּרִט. שֶׁמֹּו: עֲטָאֲלָה, יְהוָה, הִנְּחִיל, עֲטָאֲלִיָ, יְהוָה, עֲטָאֲלִיָּה. (1 Samuel 14:49).

in_greek.name: Ἀταλία
in_greek.meaning: ὁ θυγάτηρ, τοῦ θείου, ἡ δέσποινα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀταλία: ὁ θυγάτηρ, τοῦ θείου, ἡ δέσποινα. Ἀταλία ἑλληνιστί: ἀπὸ τῷ ἑβραϊκοῖς ὀνόματι עֲטָאֲלִיָּה. Ἄνθηση ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησία, ὡς ἱερὰ θυγάτηρ Ἀπ. Παῦλου.

in_latin.name: Atalia
in_latin.long_meaning: Atalia: filia dei, domina. Apatum a nominibus Hebraicis עֲטָאֲלִיָּה. Veneration in ecclesia sicut sancta Atalia Apostoli Pauli.

in_english.name: Atalia
in_english.meaning: daughter of God, lady, daughter of God's will
in_english.long_meaning: Atalia: a name of Hebrew origin, meaning daughter of God, lady, or daughter of God's will. Atalia appears in 1 Samuel 14:49. It was venerated in the early Christian church as a saintly name associated with Saint Paul.

In Christian tradition, Atalia symbolizes the idea of trust and faith in the divine providence.
data.spiritual_significance: Atalia is a name deeply rooted in spirituality, representing the belief that there is an answer to every question, a response to every prayer, and a solution to every problem. data.spiritual_symbolism: Atalia represents the strength and resilience of the ancient cedar tree, whose roots run deep and provide shelter and nourishment. This name carries the spirit of enduring faith, as Atalia is said to be a protector and source of wisdom.

biblical_reference.note: Atalia is the daughter of King Saul and the sister of Jonathan and Ishvi, and is mentioned in 1 Samuel 14:49.

historical_references.reference: Atalia I (died 42 AD) was a queen of Judea, the daughter of Herod Agrippa I. She was married to her uncle Herod Agrippa II, but when he divorced her, she was forced to flee to the Syrian city of Tyre. There she reigned as queen from about 38 to 41 AD. Her reign was marked by her persecution of the Christians in Tyre.
historical_references.context: Judea, daughter of Herod Agrippa I, ruled Tyre as queen after being divorced by her uncle Herod Agrippa II. She persecuted Christians during her reign.

historical_references.reference: Atalia II (died c. 72 AD) was a queen of the Nabateans. She was the widow of Malichus I and the mother of Malichus II. When her son was killed in battle, she assumed the throne and ruled for a short time. She was later killed in a rebellion led by her son's general, Raba'at.
historical_references.context: Nabateans, widow of Malichus I and mother of Malichus II, ruled Nabatea for a short time after her son's death. She was later killed in a rebellion led by her son's general.
